findings.title: README says the runtime flag is 'OFF by default' — the flag defaults ON; the panel is what is OFF
findings.evidence: README.md:28 `panel (v2-noc; ships in every build behind a runtime flag — OFF by default so normal frames carry zero extra pixels; ...)` vs app/main.odin:224 `app.noc_enabled = true`.
findings.detail: Grammatically the flag reads as OFF-by-default, but noc_enabled boots true (default available); only the panel/pixels default OFF. Intent is clear from context ('zero extra pixels'); wording is ambiguous for the feature's headline behavior.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword: 'the availability flag is ON by default; the panel itself is OFF until D, so normal frames carry zero extra pixels'.

findings.title: value_chip_color: NOC row highlights its default state, inverting the panel's non-default-state convention
findings.evidence: PALETTE colors mode != .Off, MOTION colors reduced_motion, SCALE colors ui_scale > 1.001, AUDIO colors snap.muted — all non-default states. `case SETTINGS_ROW_NOC: if snap.noc_enabled { return state_healthy_text(p) }` colors the DEFAULT state (noc_enabled boots true).
findings.detail: Every other row colors only its non-default state; the NOC row colors ON (the default) and leaves OFF (the non-default) unhighlighted. Cosmetic polarity inversion within one proc.
findings.recommended_fix: Return p.ink for ON and highlight OFF (or nothing), matching the other rows' color-the-non-default convention.
